building.effective: 2026-01-01 per the city's Construction Codes page. Ordinance No. 16,520 was passed and signed on December 8, 2025 and published on December 26, 2025; it is 'in full force and effect from and after its passage and publication'.
building.quote: [Construction Codes page] EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2026 - the 2024 International Building Code, 2024 International Residential Code, 2024 International Existing Building Code, and 2024 International Fire Code are adopted by the City of Des Moines. The City of Des Moines adopts the following construction codes with amendments in the Des Moines Municipal Code: 2024 International Building Code [...] State Plumbing Code (Based on the 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code) [...] | [Ordinance No. 16,520, Sec. 26-300(a)] The provisions of the International Building Code, 2024 edition, published by the International Code Council [...] are hereby adopted by reference and subject to the additions, deletions and modifications hereinafter stated as the general requirements for commercial building construction in the City of Des Moines. [...] (e) All references to the International Plumbing Code found within the IRC, IBC, and IEBC shall be interpreted to refer to the corresponding provision in the State Plumbing Code. | [Sec. 26-325] The provisions of the International Building Code (IBC), 2024 edition, are amended with the revision of the following text as stated: (1) Delete section 105.2. (2) Delete section 105.5. (3) Delete section 110.3.6. (4) Delete section 113. (5) Delete section 2901.1. (6) Delete section 2902.2. (7) Delete section 2902.6. | [certificate] passed by the City Council of said City at the meeting held on December 8, 2025 and signed by the Mayor on December 8, 2025 and published and provided by law in the Business Record on December 26, 2025.
building.chapters_8_and_10_note: Ordinance No. 16,520 and the other city amendments to the International Building Code (Sections 26-325 to 26-325.22: day care, live/work units, storm shelters, address signs, sprinklers, fire alarms, fire command center, handrails, ventilation) do not change Chapter 8 (interior finishes) or Table 1004.5 (floor area per occupant). So Section 803.9 (the room fire test for HDPE and polypropylene) and the occupant load factors apply in Des Moines as the 2024 model code prints them. Their text was read by the state agent on UpCodes' copy of the Iowa Building Code 2024 (same model code); not re-read here. The section titles of 26-325.1 to 26-325.23 not re-enacted in 16,520 were read in the city's 2023 markup of Chapter 26.
building.existing_buildings_note: Des Moines also adopts the 2024 International Existing Building Code (Sec. 26-300(c)) for repairs and alterations of existing buildings. How it applies the interior-finish fire test to replacement partitions was not read.

plumbing.name: Des Moines Plumbing Code: Municipal Code Chapter 26, Article VI, which adopts the Iowa State Plumbing Code (481 Iowa Administrative Code chapter 425: Uniform Plumbing Code with Iowa amendments) with stricter city additions
plumbing.edition: 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code as amended by Iowa (State Plumbing Code)

plumbing.quote: [Construction Codes page] State Plumbing Code (Based on the 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code) | [Chapter 26, Sec. 26-621, as printed in the city's 2023 markup] The remaining sections in this article are and represent amendments and additions to the requirements contained in the State Plumbing Code which are more restrictive than the State Plumbing Code, and where their requirements conflict with those of the State Plumbing Code, the requirements of this article shall prevail. | [481 IAC 425.2, state pack] Local jurisdictions may not adopt other plumbing codes. Local jurisdictions may adopt additional amendments provided they are stricter than the UPC as amended by this chapter
plumbing.note: The city's remaining plumbing additions (Sec. 26-628 backflow prevention, 26-632 sewer depth, 26-642 grease interceptors, 26-645 existing sewers, 26-650 to 26-655 storm drainage and pool discharge) do not touch fixture counts, toilet rooms or partitions. Sec. 26-601 as printed in the 2023 markup still names the 2021 edition and the old rule number (641 IAC 25); whether the section text has since been updated was not read (the current Municipal Code on Municode could not be opened). The state rule applies either way.

fixtures.city_amends_note: Des Moines does not change the state's toilet-count table. Its plumbing code is the State Plumbing Code, and none of the city's stricter plumbing additions deals with fixture counts. Its building code keeps Section 2902.1 and Table 2902.1 of the 2024 International Building Code (the state building code deletes the whole chapter; Des Moines deletes only Sections 2901.1, 2902.2 and 2902.6), and that table has the same ratios as the state plumbing table for the three uses: restaurants 1 per 75, business 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 after that, educational 1 per 50, half of the occupants counted for each sex and fractions rounded up. Because the city deletes Section 2902.2, the rule on separate men's and women's rooms and its exceptions comes from the State Plumbing Code (422.2: 10 or fewer in any use, 50 or fewer in business and mercantile, or a shared room with every toilet and urinal in a privacy compartment). The state pack's twelve worked examples stand.

city_table_read.note: 2024 International Building Code Chapter 29 read on UpCodes' copy of the Wyoming Building Code 2024 ('adopts without amendments'), a secondary copy; codes.iccsafe.org returned HTTP 403.
city_table_read.quote: [2902.1] Plumbing fixtures shall be provided in the minimum number as shown in Table 2902.1 based on the actual use of the building or space. [...] The number of occupants shall be determined by this code. [2902.1.1] To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. [...] Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 2902.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. [...] Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. [Table 2902.1] Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts d | 1 per 75 | 1 per 75 | 1 per 200 [...] 2 Business | Buildings for the transaction of business, nonmedical professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, light industrial and similar uses | 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50 | 1 per 40 for the first 80 and 1 per 80 for the remainder exceeding 80 [...] 3 Educational | Educational facilities | 1 per 50 | 1 per 50 [2902.1.2] Single-user toilet facilities and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet facilities and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Not redone: the city does not amend the counts, so the state pack's examples apply (office 1/1, 2/2, 3/3, 5/5; restaurant 1/1, 1/1, 2/2, 3/3; school 1/1, 1/1, 2/2, 4/4 at 50, 100, 200 and 400 occupants).

permit.exempt_list_quote: [Sec. 26-301(a)] Building permits are required as identified in IBC chapter 1, part 2; IRC chapter 1, part 2; and IEBC Chapter 1, part 2. [Sec. 26-302. Building permit exemptions] (a) A building permit shall not be required for the following: (1) One-story detached accessory buildings used as tool or storage sheds, playhouses, pet shelters, and similar uses [...] provided the floor area does not exceed 120 square feet [...] (2) Chain link or wire fences four feet or less in height and all other fences three feet or less in height. (3) Movable cases, counters, and partitions not over five feet nine inches in height. (4) Playground equipment. (5) Retaining walls, which retain no more than four feet of unbalanced fill [...] (6) Retaining walls which are part of a public improvement project regulated by the City Engineer. (7) Tanks supported directly upon grade if the capacity does not exceed 5,000 gallons [...] (8) Platforms, walks, and driveways not more than 30 inches above grade and not over any basement or story below. (9) Painting, papering, and similar finish work. (10) Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery. (11) Window awnings supported by an exterior wall of one and two family dwellings [...] (12) Minor maintenance and repair work that is deemed by the building official not to affect structural strength, safety, fire resistance, or sanitation, provided that no such work shall be performed in a manner contrary to any provisions of the building code or any other laws. (13) Installation, alteration or repair of generation, transmission, distribution or metering or other related equipment that is under the ownership and control of public service agencies by established right. (b) Unless otherwise exempted, separate plumbing, electrical and mechanical permits will be required when appropriate for the exempted items in subsection (a) of this section. (c) Exemption from the permit requirements of this section shall not be deemed to grant authorization for any work to be done in any manner in violation of the provisions of the building code or any other laws or ordinances of this jurisdiction. | [Permit exemption policy for minor maintenance and repair, effective 7-1-2023] The following work shall be considered minor maintenance and repair that is exempt from permit under municipal code section 26-302(a)(11). Reroofing that does not involve alteration of roof sheathing, decking or framing members. Residing of walls [...] Window replacement that meets all of the following criteria [...] Tuckpointing/mortar repair. Replacing decking boards on open wood decks. Replacing non-fire rated doors/frames with doors of same swing and size. Installation of foundation repair systems [...] Sheetrock and plaster repair. [...] Items exempt from permit are still required to meet current code requirements. Contact Permit and Development Center Staff with questions.
permit.partitions_named_note: Toilet partitions are not named in Sec. 26-302 or in the city's minor-repair policy. The only partitions on the list are 'movable' ones not over 5 feet 9 inches; toilet partitions are fixed to the floor, wall or ceiling. Whether a like-for-like replacement counts as 'similar finish work' or as minor maintenance and repair is for the building official. Sec. 26-302 was read in the city's 2023 markup of Chapter 26 (the section was last amended by Ordinance 16,224 in February 2023, and Ordinances 16,317, 16,412 and 16,520 do not amend it); the policy cites the minor-repair item as (a)(11) while the markup numbers it (a)(12). The current Municode text was not opened.

restrooms_city.quote: No city ordinance on single-user restroom signs or shared all-gender rooms was found. Des Moines' building code keeps Section 2902.1.2 of the 2024 International Building Code (single-user rooms 'shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex'), which matches the state plumbing rule, and deletes Section 2902.2, so the state plumbing code's rule on separate and shared rooms applies.
restrooms_city.note: One web search and the Chapter 26 text read turned up no city restroom rule. The city's civil rights chapter (Chapter 62) was not read.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Des Moines job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Des Moines and Iowa rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Des Moines insurance offices, state government buildings, schools and distribution centers, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Des Moines' building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Iowa's plumbing rules, which Des Moines enforces, set the number of toilets by how many people use the building, and the city's own building rules carry the same numbers. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Des Moines requires a building permit for work covered by its building rules unless the work is on the city's exempt list. The list covers movable partitions no taller than 5 feet 9 inches, painting, papering and similar finish work, and minor maintenance and repair that the building official judges not to affect structure, safety, fire resistance or sanitation. It doesn't name toilet partitions fixed to the floor or wall, so ask the Des Moines Permit and Development Center (515-283-4200) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the Des Moines Permit and Development Center
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, Des Moines' building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Your architect or the Permit and Development Center sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Des Moines licenses electrical, mechanical, plumbing and sign contractors, and its code sets no city license for general contractors. Iowa requires construction contractors, subcontractors included, who earn $2,000 or more a year from construction to register with the state each year. Confirm what your project needs with the Des Moines Permit and Development Center. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor who earns $2,000 or more a year from construction work must be registered with the State of Iowa.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Iowa has no state wage law for public jobs, so a set wage applies only on work paid for with federal money, where federal law sets it by county. For a carpenter on building work in Polk County that is $24.93 an hour plus $11.17 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 7% in Des Moines: 6% state and a 1% local option tax. Ankeny and Waukee have no local option tax, so the rate there is 6%.
page.buyers_extra: - **Insurance and government office buildings:** overhead braced or floor-to-ceiling stalls for large multi-stall restrooms, in a finish that matches the building standard.
sources: - Codes Des Moines enforces: City of Des Moines, Permit and Development Center, [Construction Codes](https://www.dsm.city/departments/development_services/permit_development_center/construction_codes.php) (2024 International Building Code and 2024 International Existing Building Code in effect January 1, 2026; State Plumbing Code based on the 2024 Uniform Plumbing Code) and [Ordinance No. 16,520](https://councildocs.dsm.city/ordinances/16,520.pdf), passed December 8, 2025, amending Municipal Code Chapter 26, Sections 26-300 and 26-325 (the city deletes Sections 105.2, 2901.1, 2902.2 and 2902.6 of the International Building Code and reads its plumbing references as the State Plumbing Code; Chapter 8 and Table 1004.5 are unchanged). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Toilet counts in Des Moines: the State Plumbing Code applies ([481 Iowa Administrative Code chapter 425](https://www.legis.iowa.gov/docs/iac/chapter/481.425.pdf), which bars local plumbing codes other than stricter amendments); the city's own additions, Municipal Code Chapter 26, Article VI, Sections 26-621 to 26-655, read in the [city's 2023 markup of Chapter 26](https://cms2.revize.com/revize/desmoines/CHAP.%2026%20-%202023%20Updates%20-%20Markup%20Version.pdf), do not deal with fixture counts. The city also keeps Section 2902.1 and Table 2902.1 of the 2024 International Building Code, which give the same ratios; read on a secondary copy, [UpCodes, 2024 International Building Code, Chapter 29](https://up.codes/viewer/wyoming/ibc-2024/chapter/29/plumbing-systems). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Permits in Des Moines: Municipal Code Sections 26-301 and 26-302 (building permit exemptions), read in the [city's 2023 markup of Chapter 26](https://cms2.revize.com/revize/desmoines/CHAP.%2026%20-%202023%20Updates%20-%20Markup%20Version.pdf), and the Permit and Development Center's [Permit exemption policy for minor maintenance and repair (effective July 1, 2023)](https://www.dsm.city/Documents/Departments/Development%20Services/Permit%20Development%20Center/Construction%20Codes/Minor%20Repair-%20Permit%20Exemption%20Policy%207-1-23.pdf). Office and phone: [Permit and Development Center](https://www.dsm.city/departments/development_services/permit_development_center/index.php), 515-283-4200. Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax in Des Moines: Iowa Department of Revenue, [Local Option Rates and Sunsets](https://revenue.iowa.gov/media/195/download?inline) (rates effective July 1, 2026; Polk County, Des Moines: 1% local option tax since July 1, 2019, total 7%), linked from [Local Option Sales Tax](https://revenue.iowa.gov/taxes/tax-guidance/sales-use-excise-tax/local-option-sales-tax); City of Des Moines, [Local Option](https://www.dsm.city/government/strategic_efforts/local_option/index.php). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Polk County carpenter rate: [federal wage determination IA20260071, modification 1, Building](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/IA20260071/1), published May 18, 2026 (Carpenter, includes drywall hanging: $24.93 an hour, $11.17 fringes). Checked 2026-11-24.
page.official_names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, adopted in Iowa by 481 IAC 301.18 (alternative: 2024 International Building Code Chapter 11 with ICC A117.1-2017); Des Moines Municipal Code Chapter 26, Article III (2024 International Building Code and 2024 International Existing Building Code with Des Moines amendments, Ordinance No. 16,520, in effect January 1, 2026; Section 803.9, Table 1004.5 and Table 2902.1) and Article VI (Des Moines Plumbing Code); Iowa State Plumbing Code, 481 IAC chapter 425 (2024 Uniform Plumbing Code with Iowa amendments, in force March 26, 2025; Table 422.1 and Sections 422.2 and 422.8); NFPA 286 for HDPE.
notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether a like-for-like replacement of anchored toilet partitions in a commercial restroom needs a Des Moines building permit (Permit and Development Center, 515-283-4200, permits@dmgov.org).

Municipal Code Sections 26-301, 26-302 and the plumbing article were read in the city's own 2023 markup of Chapter 26, not on Municode (it would not open): check the current text of Section 26-302 once in a browser. The city's minor-repair policy cites item (a)(11) where the markup numbers it (a)(12).

The fire test for solid plastic partitions and the floor area per person come from the 2024 model building code, which Des Moines adopts without changing those parts; the text was read on secondary copies (UpCodes), not on codes.iccsafe.org.
How Des Moines applies the fire test to replacement partitions in an existing building (it uses the 2024 existing-building code for alterations) was not read: ask the Permit and Development Center.
The federal carpenter rate for Polk County ($24.93 plus $11.17) comes from a 2016 survey and is below the area's current median wage; recheck the determination on sam.gov before launch.

Sales tax: the 7% rate was read in the Department of Revenue's July 1, 2026 workbook. The part of Des Moines in Warren County was not looked up separately; the Department's address lookup is at tax-mapper.iowa.gov.
